paragraphs.source_en: “You take naps too? That is splendid. If one can sleep in the afternoon and sleep at night as well, nothing could be better.” Mr. Meitei went on as usual in his carefree way, and apparently feeling that this was not enough, added a few more words: “A man of my constitution simply does not care to nap in the daytime. But when I see Kushami fast asleep every time I come here, I quite envy him. Of course this heat is hard on anyone with a weak stomach, would you not say? On a day like today, even a sturdy person finds it a burden to carry a head on his shoulders. And yet, since the head is there on one’s shoulders, one cannot very well tear it off, can one?” It seemed that, unusually for him, Mr. Meitei was at a loss over how to dispose of the head. “Madam, you have yet another heavy thing sitting on top of your head, so you can hardly be expected to sit upright. The weight of that chignon alone must make you want to lie down.”
